observations.observation: Assertions cover encrypted writes, untrusted import provenance, explicit invoice-link consent, stale scan/preview/unlock revocation, payload-free refresh, partial amount summary limits, and privacy reveal. Receipt archive fixtures use ordinary current timestamps; these files do not assert the out-of-Date-range ingress/render criterion for CUSTODY-02. No runtime result claimed.

Assertions cover discarded/changed previews, partial cross-chain import outcomes, lost write acknowledgements, lifecycle/session locks, export cleanup, stale CAS/wipe/rotation handling, keyed lookup/AAD binding, and typed tag payloads. Latest TagArchive test delta explicitly checks idle authority suspension and removal of archive forms; older baseline asserts field clearing with retained session.

Assertions preserve endpoint confidentiality by stripping session-only primary/secondary selections from storage and exchange; credential detection is explicitly heuristic and consent remains slot/chain specific. These isolated storage/exchange tests do not demonstrate that private scanning receives the same-tab endpoints. UI privacy is persisted separately in the latest privacy variants. No new production finding and no runtime result.

observations.area: Settings UI and scoped network operations
observations.observation: Settings tests assert explicit endpoint/trust selection, import preview invalidation, failed-save behavior, session-only omission, profile acknowledgment, cross-tab changes and stale RPC-test results. They stop before exercising session-only endpoint selection from private Scan. Network operation tests assert exact/prefix destination limits, most-specific grant revocation, incomplete profile refusal, adapter dispatch revocation and redirect refusal. Loopback server test code was read only; no listeners or probes were run.

observations.area: Network authority, export RPC and scan transport
observations.observation: Source asserts per-action capability and selected-endpoint binding, exact payment-export address/method binding, clock validity, context/request expiry, lifecycle cancellation, bounded body disposal, no fallback, and privacy-policy validation. networkAuthorization.test.ts:140-147 directly supplies a session-only URL to authority, so this does not exercise Scan selection from persisted settings. Client/scheduler tests assert cancellation after jitter and late responses, independent request budgets and window caps. Sweep state tests assert journal CAS and unknown-status preservation. No new production finding and no runtime result.

observations.area: Browser transport package and scan privacy/indexer
observations.observation: Complete mixed transport core test body retained because it also tests the active browser guards/onion/settings/fetch adapters. Package selection parser defaults are separate from application network authority strict validity checks. Tests assert stream byte/deadline cleanup, redirect isolation, fixed-window shaping, padding and provider-limit splitting. Indexer tests explicitly retain the omitted-record limitation; header continuity/witness assertions do not prove log completeness. Test fixture utility includes unused PIR helpers incidentally; no production scope expansion.

observations.area: Scan-source, portable vault and metadata package tests
observations.observation: Scan range/padding/validation tests assert public-bound request shaping, byte/record budgets, late cancellation and normalized records; no new finding. Portable-parity is an import wrapper plus bounded-header checks: its import list is not coverage for the imported tests (remaining reconciliation suites are explicitly pending). Amount-summary tests retain seller/chain/asset/invoice/provenance binding, duplicate invariance, contradiction refusal and exact bigint totals. Metadata release/guard tests cover the used padding primitive and common guards; unused catalogue/release features were incidentally read in those mixed files.

Full buffer/ledger/verify bodies and fixture utility read. Active funding-guard assertions reject known-wallet/destination funding and malformed addresses. Destination-ledger assertions cover per-chain isolation, explicit reuse, own/protocol destination refusal, index conflicts/exhaustion, strict import shape and non-aliasing serialization. Shared testnet guard and mixed verification tests assert transfer-log normalization, bounded address-free query shapes, incomplete-range reporting and failure when secure randomness or required batch support is absent. Deterministic scalar/RNG fixtures are explicitly test data. Incidental unused feature assertions are not an expansion of browser production scope. No runtime result or new production finding.
